 T.J. Watt fine, Rico Dowdle questionable to play for Steelers vs. Saints
 By Chris Adamski 2 Min Read 
 • Oct. 23, 2026 
 | 1 day ago 
-->
 Go Ad-Free today 
 Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebackers Nick Herbig (left) T.J. Watt (center) work out at the Le Meridien Arc de Triomphe hotel in Paris. Watt was given the official green light to play in Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints. (Karl Roser | Pittsburgh Steelers) 
 PARIS — In an apparent sign of how minor the calf injury that afflicted T.J. Watt this week is, when Watt was asked how he was feeling Friday he instinctively discussed the jet lag from the long overnight flight to France.
 “I feel really good, honestly,” Watt said after participating in a walkthrough in a hotel ballroom Friday. “I just tried to hydrate as much as possible. I was able to sleep on the plane, just hit an espresso, so I should be good to go.”
 That comes as a relief to the Steelers, who Thursday listed Watt as a limited participant in practice because of a calf injury. Via the injury report Friday, Watt was officially given the green light to play against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday at Stade de France.
 Also cleared despite being on the injury report were fellow outside linebacker Alex Highsmith (groin) and safety Jalen Ramsey, the latter of whom has played the past three games despite a wrist fracture.
 Dowdle questionable 
 Running back Rico Dowdle is listed as questionable to play Sunday because of a knee injury that had him listed as limited in practices throughout the week.
 Dowdle returned from a three-game absence because of a dislocated toe and played in last week’s win at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He is listed this week as having a knee ailment.
 Also questionable is veteran safety DeShon Elliott, who is slated to come off of the injured reserve list after recovery from knee surgery.
 No Echols, Skowronek 
 Neither reserve cornerback Brandin Echols nor depth wide receiver Ben Skowronek will play against the Saints. Neither of the pair of core special-teamers participated in a practice this week, and neither made the trip to Paris.
 With Skowronek out and two other receivers on IR (Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson), the Steelers against the Bucs called up two receivers from the practice squad. They are expected to do that again Sunday.
 Echols suffered a hamstring injury against the Bucs, and Skowronek will miss a second straight game because of a calf injury.
